items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 34:1
items.html: The discernment of YESHSUT, which are from the Chazeh downward of AVI, are discerned as the discernment of the belly of AVI, which protrudes and goes out outside the body of AVI, because the body of AVI is from the discernment of covered Hassadim, upon which no restriction rules. However, Abba brought Ima out for the sake of her son, because YESHSUT, who are Ima, received into themselves the discernment of the second restriction, in order to draw correction and Mochin to ZON, as is known. Therefore it is discerned that this protrusion, in which YESHSUT draw away to the discernment of outside the body of AVI, is not because of themselves, for even YESHSUT are the discernment of Bina like AVI, and no restriction applies in them. Rather, the protrusion outward — that is, the restriction — is in the manner of a pregnant woman, whose belly protrudes outward and draws away from her body because of the fetus lying in her belly, and not because of herself. Likewise, since YESHSUT are the root of ZON, and ZON are with them in the discernment of impregnation, therefore YESHSUT protrude and draw away from their own body, that is, from covered Hassadim, and they draw revealed Hassadim for the sake of ZON, who are the fetus; through this they were also restricted, because therefore the second restriction also rules in them. (Item 84).
